chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That Ali (peace be upon him) prayed two rak'ahs during the solar eclipse, with four prostrations and four bowings: he stood and recited, then bowed, then raised his head and recited, then bowed, then stood and supplicated like his standing [in the first rak'ah], then prostrated two prostrations, then stood and did the same as he did in the first [rak'ah] in his recitation, standing, bowing, and prostration, identically.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali (peace be upon him) perform the solar eclipse prayer in terms of rak'ahs, bowings, and prostrations?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the Sunnah of Imam Ali (peace be upon him) regarding the specific structure of the solar eclipse prayer, emphasizing a unique two-rak'ah format with four bowings and four prostrations. The detailed narration highlights the precision of the ritual, where the second rak'ah mirrors the first in recitation, bowing, and prostration, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imams' role in preserving and clarifying prophetic practices. This specific mode of prayer serves as a practical model for believers to seek divine protection and reflect on the signs of Allah during celestial phenomena.
